brief.title: California SB 253/SB 261 climate disclosure rollout and challenges
brief.summary: California's corporate climate-disclosure regime is taking effect. CARB's initial regulation was approved Oct 12, 2026, and the first SB 253 Scope 1 and 2 emissions reports are due Nov 10, 2026. Meanwhile, SB 261 remains enjoined pending a Ninth Circuit merits ruling, and the OCC is pressing CARB to exempt national banks.
brief.origin: SB 253 (Scope 1–3 GHG reporting for firms over $1B in revenue doing business in California) and SB 261 (biennial climate-risk reports for firms over $500M) passed in 2023. The US Chamber of Commerce and co-plaintiffs challenged both laws in federal court. In Aug 2025 the district court denied a preliminary injunction. The plaintiffs then sought an injunction pending appeal from the Ninth Circuit in Sept 2025. On Nov 18, 2025, the Ninth Circuit enjoined SB 261 only, effectively suspending its Jan 1, 2026 deadline, and let SB 253 proceed. In Dec 2025 CARB said it would not enforce the SB 261 deadline and opened a voluntary public docket for SB 261 reports. Oral argument followed on Jan 9, 2026. CARB adopted its Initial Regulation on Feb 26, 2026, setting annual fees of about $3,106 per company under SB 253 and $1,403 under SB 261. It submitted the rule to OAL in May, withdrew it in June (which moved the first deadline from Aug 10 to Nov 10), and resubmitted in Sept. OAL approved the rule on Oct 12, 2026 (17 CCR §§96070–96077).
brief.causes: California is using state law to force emissions and climate-risk disclosure from large public and private companies, filling a gap in federal mandates. Opponents argue the laws compel speech on the state's preferred climate views (First Amendment). The litigation also raises Commerce Clause, Supremacy Clause and Clean Air Act claims, and a separate challenge argues SB 261 is preempted by federal securities law. The federal bank regulator objects that applying the laws to federally chartered banks conflicts with federal supervision and safety-and-soundness rules and burdens smaller banks. CARB has softened year one to keep the timeline credible: it accepts already-collected data, uses consolidated parent reports, and, per ESG Today, does not require assurance in year one.

actors.name: California Air Resources Board (CARB), Chair Lauren Sanchez
actors.role: Writes and enforces the implementing rules, sets deadlines and fees, and maintains the list of likely covered companies
actors.stake: Launching SB 253 on schedule with a lighter first year, and reviving SB 261 if the courts allow

actors.name: US Chamber of Commerce and co-plaintiffs (CalChamber, American Farm Bureau Federation, LA County and Central Valley business federations, Western Growers)
actors.role: Challenging both laws in the Ninth Circuit; reminded the court in Oct 2026 that its decision is still pending
actors.stake: Having both laws struck down or blocked, avoiding compliance cost and compelled disclosure

actors.name: Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals
actors.role: Has enjoined SB 261 pending appeal; merits decision outstanding more than nine months after argument
actors.stake: Its ruling decides whether either law survives and could disrupt the Nov 10 deadline

actors.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Comptroller Jonathan Gould
actors.role: Oct 29, 2026 letter asking CARB to exempt national banks and federal savings associations, or to clarify that they need not comply
actors.stake: Federal primacy over bank supervision; it has floated preemption but taken no formal preemptive action

actors.name: Bank trade groups (BPI, ABA)
actors.role: BPI commented on the 2027 rules (Sept 4, 2026); both amplify the OCC's concerns
actors.stake: Narrower scope and lower compliance burden for banks

actors.name: ExxonMobil
actors.role: Separate suit against the laws, with its injunction request paused pending the Chamber appeal
actors.stake: Same relief as the Chamber plaintiffs

actors.name: Covered companies (CARB preliminary list: more than 4,000 likely in scope)
actors.role: Must file Scope 1 and 2 reports by Nov 10, 2026 and prepare Scope 3 for 2027
actors.stake: Compliance cost, data readiness, supplier data collection, and litigation risk on disclosed figures

brief.status: SB 253 is in force. Scope 1 and 2 reports are due Nov 10, 2026, with first-year enforcement flexibility, use of existing data and consolidated parent reports. Scope 3 begins in 2027. SB 261 remains enjoined, with no new deadline set; voluntary reports can be posted to CARB's docket. The Ninth Circuit merits ruling is pending and could come at any time. The OCC has sent only a letter, not a formal preemption. It is unknown whether CARB will respond or grant a bank exemption, and analysts advise banks not to stop preparing. Coverage counts are inconsistent: ESG Today cites more than 4,000 companies, while Watershed estimated about 2,600 for SB 253 and about 4,100 for SB 261.
watch: Nov 10, 2026: first SB 253 Scope 1 and 2 reporting deadline; watch filing volume and quality on CARB's systems
Ninth Circuit merits decision in Chamber of Commerce v. Sanchez (timing unknown), which could revive SB 261 or enjoin SB 253
CARB response to the OCC's Oct 29 letter, and any formal OCC preemption action
CARB's 2027 rulemaking: annual Nov 10 deadline, Scope 3 phase-in for five categories, assurance standards, and a fixed GHG Protocol version

research.question: Does mandatory state-level emissions disclosure change reported emissions, energy sourcing or decarbonization actions among private firms that previously did not disclose, relative to firms just below the $1B threshold?
research.shock: Oct 12, 2026 OAL approval and Nov 10, 2026 first SB 253 deadline (revenue-threshold discontinuity)
research.data: CARB preliminary covered-entity list and filed SB 253 reports; CDP responses; EPA GHGRP facility data for pre/post comparison

research.question: How do Scope 3 requirements starting in 2027 propagate upstream, for example through supplier data requests, supplier selection or switching, and costs borne by small suppliers outside the law's scope?
research.shock: 2027 Scope 3 phase-in (five categories) announced at CARB's Jul 21, 2026 workshop
research.data: Supplier-relationship data (e.g., FactSet Revere, Bloomberg SPLC) linked to the covered-firm list; supplier sustainability surveys; CDP supply chain program

research.question: Does regulatory uncertainty from litigation and federal preemption threats change disclosure quality and timing, comparing the enjoined SB 261 with SB 253, or national versus state-chartered banks?
research.shock: Nov 18, 2025 Ninth Circuit SB 261 injunction; Oct 29, 2026 OCC letter
research.data: Voluntary SB 261 reports on CARB's public docket; bank charter type from FDIC/OCC; SB 253 filing timing and content
